column1: # subsdk0 is NintendoSDK_movie (main imports from it)
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the game's config caps Unreal at 30 (FrameRateLimit=30 in DefaultGameUserSettings.ini, which sets t.MaxFPS, and nvn.SyncInterval=2 in SwitchEngine.ini, the present
# interval 2 it asks for); the host writes t.MaxFPS 60 and nvn.SyncInterval 1 into its console variables (hle_fpslock.c), so the game asks for present interval 1 itself. Unreal steps the game by
# the time that really passed. DM_FPS_TARGET=30 (Documents/env.txt on the iPhone) keeps the game's 30 and saves power
# Dynamic resolution: Unreal's controller (main+0x3140180) takes the median of RHIGetGPUFrameCycles (main+0x373bd80), the sum of the frame's begin / end timestamp-report
# deltas divided by 615,384,615 ticks a second (main+0x372ae1c, the constant at main+0x6205fe8), and lowers the resolution above r.DynamicResolution.MaxTimeBudget (33 ms).
# With the host's 19.2 MHz counter ticks it read a 28 ms frame as 0.74 ms (read from the running game, main+0x84eda28) and never lowered it; with 614.4 MHz ticks it reads
# a 3D game: D-pad, right stick (camera) and L3 / R3 on the iPhone's virtual gamepad
# Unreal Engine 4.18: nninitStartup takes one address region for the whole engine (16 GB by default), which a NumberLineAllocator (main+0x177c4d0) hands out; the game's argument
# -SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize= caps it, in MB up to 4095 (main+0x177c440: atoi, and a larger number is taken as bytes; 4224 gave a 4 KB region and a crash in the allocator's
# Compaction at boot). Two cuts on the SDK 7.3.2 build (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py) put it 64 MB into the alias region: the node area 62 MB instead of 1 GB, and regions of 1 GB and more
# 32 MB aligned instead of 1 GB. Engage's 5 GB block: 256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region (the game sets no heap)
# The engine's global shaders (Engine/GlobalShaderCache-GLSL_SWITCH.bin), the engine's own materials and the game's. Unreal Engine 4.18 keeps every shader inline in the cooked packages,
# zlib-compressed, in paks whose blocks are LZ5-compressed; the NSP script decodes them on the Mac with the game's own LZ5 (uepak.py, shader_split.py ue_legacy_jobs, DM_OODLE_SERVE)
# Android: the paks' LZ5 files are decoded by the game's own LZ5 on the Android device instead (porter/pipeline.py device_ue_legacy, hle_oodle.c ue_group_job), and only the files that can hold a
# The skinning shaders read their bone matrices from texture buffers with 1D integer fetches the answer table has no type for: as 2D rows they read the dummy
# view and every skinned character was invisible (the field showed only the hero's sword). Translated as texture buffers instead (dm/android/tools/shader_vk.py)
